title: Google Translate
description: Open Google Translate on the screen that fits the request — a live spoken conversation, the camera, a transcription of someone speaking, or dictation — with the languages already set, through the googletranslate: links the app publishes for its own shortcuts. Google Translate reports nothing back, so a receipt says the screen was opened, never that anything was heard, seen, or translated.
setup: Install Google Translate (com.google.android.apps.translate); these actions pin its main activity and fail if the app is absent.
Let Google Translate use the microphone, and the camera for the camera action. It asks the first time each screen runs, and EVA cannot grant either.
Download the languages inside Google Translate to translate them without a network connection.

tool.name: live_translate
tool.title: Start live translation
tool.description: Open Google Translate's Live translate screen, which listens to speech and translates between two languages. Choose audio_mode: conversation for a two-sided exchange read aloud in both directions, listening to follow someone speaking without replying to them, or text to read the translation instead of hearing it. Give languages as Google Translate's codes: en, es, fr, de, it, pt, pt-BR, nl, ru, uk, pl, tr, ar, he, hi, fa, th, vi, id, ja, ko, zh-CN, zh-TW. Use it when the user wants to talk with, or listen to, someone in another language, not to translate text EVA already has. A code Google Translate does not recognize is discarded and the app keeps whichever languages it last used. Opening the screen is all this reports; the microphone, the languages the app settles on, and every translation are unverified.

target_language.description: Google Translate code for the language to translate into, such as es, ja, or pt-BR.

source_language.description: Google Translate code for the language being spoken, such as en. Omit it, or pass auto, to let the app detect the speaker's language.

audio_mode.description: How the screen should run. conversation is a two-way exchange with both sides spoken aloud, and is what EVA sends when this is omitted. listening follows one person speaking without answering them. text shows the translation without speaking it.

press_to_talk.description: Wait for a tap before each turn instead of listening hands-free. Google Translate's own preference can still force this on.

receipts.success: Live translate opened in Google Translate. Whether it is listening is not verified.
receipts.handlerMissing: Google Translate is not installed, or the installed version does not have the Live translate screen this link opens.

tool.name: camera_translate
tool.title: Translate with the camera
tool.description: Open Google Translate's camera, which overlays a translation on whatever the phone is pointed at. Use it for a sign, a menu, a label, or any other printed text in front of the user, not for text EVA already has. A code Google Translate does not recognize is discarded and the app keeps whichever languages it last used. Opening the screen is all this reports; the camera, the languages the app settles on, and every translation are unverified.

target_language.description: Google Translate code for the language to translate into, such as es, ja, or pt-BR. Codes: en, es, fr, de, it, pt, pt-BR, nl, ru, uk, pl, tr, ar, he, hi, fa, th, vi, id, ja, ko, zh-CN, zh-TW.

source_language.description: Google Translate code for the language being translated from, such as en. Omit it, or pass auto, to let the app detect it.

receipts.success: Camera translation opened in Google Translate. What it captures is not verified.
receipts.handlerMissing: Google Translate is not installed, or the installed version does not have the screen this link opens.

tool.name: transcribe
tool.title: Transcribe and translate speech
tool.description: Open Google Translate's Transcribe screen, which listens continuously to one speaker and builds a running translation of what they say. Use it for a lecture, an announcement, or anyone talking at length in one language; use live translation instead for a two-sided conversation. Opening the screen is all this reports; nothing about what is heard or transcribed is verified.

target_language.description: Google Translate code for the language to translate into, such as es, ja, or pt-BR. Codes: en, es, fr, de, it, pt, pt-BR, nl, ru, uk, pl, tr, ar, he, hi, fa, th, vi, id, ja, ko, zh-CN, zh-TW.

source_language.description: Google Translate code for the language being translated from, such as en. Omit it, or pass auto, to let the app detect it.

receipts.success: Transcribe opened in Google Translate. What it hears is not verified.
receipts.handlerMissing: Google Translate is not installed, or the installed version does not have the screen this link opens.

tool.name: dictate
tool.title: Dictate a translation
tool.description: Open Google Translate's dictation screen, where the user speaks once and the app shows and speaks the translation, ready to copy or share. Use it to produce one translated phrase the user wants to keep or send, rather than to hold a conversation. Opening the screen is all this reports; the microphone and the translation itself are unverified.
